prs.title: fix(shared): make McpError and UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe on v1.x
prs.author: NishchayMahor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Python's default pickle path calls cls(*self.args) to reconstruct exceptions. MCPError.__init__ expects an ErrorData object, but self.args contains only the message string (set by super().__init__(error.message)), so unpickling crashes with a TypeError. UrlElicitationRequiredError compounds this because its constructor signature (elicitations, message=None) doesn't match the MCPError-set args tuple at all. All three PRs add __reduce__ overrides to fix this on the same file (src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py). (3 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2703 is the only one that adds __reduce__ to the base McpError class (returning (cls, (self.error,))), which is the root fix — without it McpError itself is not pickle-safe regardless of what subclasses do. It also adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, making the fix complete for the whole hierarchy. PR #2555 patches only the subclass and leaves the base class broken; PR #2478 introduces an indirect _restore_mcp_error helper instead of the simpler direct __reduce__ approach. members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2703: Python's default pickle path calls cls(*self.args) to reconstruct exceptions. UrlElicitationRequiredError compounds this because its constructor signature (elicitations, message=None) doesn't match the MCPError-set args tuple at all. All three PRs add __reduce__ overrides to fix this on the same file (src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py).

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Python's default pickle path calls cls(*self.args) to reconstruct exceptions. MCPError.__init__ expects an ErrorData object, but self.args contains only the message string (set by super().__init__(error.message)), so unpickling crashes with a TypeError. UrlElicitationRequiredError compounds this because its constructor signature (elicitations, message=None) doesn't match the MCPError-set args tuple at all. All three PRs add __reduce__ overrides to fix this on the same file (src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py). (3 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2703 is the only one that adds __reduce__ to the base McpError class (returning (cls, (self.error,))), which is the root fix — without it McpError itself is not pickle-safe regardless of what subclasses do. It also adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, making the fix complete for the whole hierarchy. PR #2555 patches only the subclass and leaves the base class broken; PR #2478 introduces an indirect _restore_mcp_error helper instead of the simpler direct __reduce__ approach. The test coverage from PR #2555 should be ported into #2703 before merge.

members.title: fix: make ClientSessionGroup streamable HTTP errors catchable
members.author: VrtxOmega
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP connection errors in ClientSessionGroup are not being surfaced or catchable. Both PRs touch the `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` methods of `ClientSessionGroup` in `session_group.py` to address this. PR #2711 removes `# pragma: no cover` from those methods (making the code paths testable), while PR #2637 changes the `__aexit__` teardown from a concurrent `anyio` task group to a sequential loop (to preserve AnyIO task contexts and let errors propagate), and removes the `anyio` import. clusters.pick_reason: PR #2703 is the only one that adds __reduce__ to the base McpError class (returning (cls, (self.error,))), which is the root fix — without it McpError itself is not pickle-safe regardless of what subclasses do. It also adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, making the fix complete for the whole hierarchy. PR #2555 patches only the subclass and leaves the base class broken; PR #2478 introduces an indirect _restore_mcp_error helper instead of the simpler direct __reduce__ approach. The test coverage from PR #2555 should be ported into #2703 before merge.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2703: Python's default pickle path calls cls(*self.args) to reconstruct exceptions. MCPError.__init__ expects an ErrorData object, but self.args contains only the message string (set by super().__init__(error.message)), so unpickling crashes with a TypeError. UrlElicitationRequiredError compounds this because its constructor signature (elicitations, message=None) doesn't match the MCPError-set args tuple at all. All three PRs add __reduce__ overrides to fix this on the same file (src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py).

members.title: fix: make ClientSessionGroup streamable HTTP errors catchable
members.author: VrtxOmega
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP connection errors in ClientSessionGroup are not being surfaced or catchable. Both PRs touch the `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` methods of `ClientSessionGroup` in `session_group.py` to address this. PR #2711 removes `# pragma: no cover` from those methods (making the code paths testable), while PR #2637 changes the `__aexit__` teardown from a concurrent `anyio` task group to a sequential loop (to preserve AnyIO task contexts and let errors propagate), and removes the `anyio` import. Together they address the same root cause from complementary angles — one fixes runtime behavior, the other enables test coverage of those same paths. (2 PRs)
